source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Magnets and Magnetic Materials
points: A **magnet** attracts certain materials. **Magnetic materials** are attracted to magnets: **iron, nickel, cobalt** (and steel).
**Non-magnetic materials** are not attracted: wood, plastic, rubber, paper, cloth, most non-iron metals.
Natural magnet = **magnetite (lodestone)**; magnets can also be made artificially in shapes (bar, horseshoe, ring, U-shaped).

sections.heading: 2. Poles of a Magnet
points: Every magnet has **two poles: North (N) and South (S)**.
Attraction is **strongest at the poles**.
**Poles always exist in pairs** — if a magnet is broken, each piece still has an N and an S pole.
A magnet's poles **cannot be separated** (no single isolated pole).

sections.heading: 3. Attraction and Repulsion
points: **Like poles repel** (N–N or S–S push apart).
**Unlike poles attract** (N–S pull together).
**Repulsion** is the sure test of a magnet (attraction alone is not, since a magnet also attracts plain iron).

sections.heading: 4. Freely Suspended Magnet and the Compass
points: A **freely suspended magnet always comes to rest in the North–South direction**.
The pole pointing north = **north-seeking (North) pole**; the other = South pole.
This is the principle of the **magnetic compass**, used to **find directions**.
The **Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet**.

sections.heading: 5. Making and Caring for Magnets
points: A magnet can be made from an iron piece by **stroking it repeatedly in one direction** with a bar magnet.
Magnets **lose magnetism** if heated, hammered or dropped; store bar magnets in **pairs with unlike poles together** and keep away from electronic devices.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Magnetic materials: iron, nickel, cobalt (attracted); wood/plastic/paper are non-magnetic.
Two poles: North & South; force strongest at the poles.
Like poles repel; unlike poles attract; repulsion is the sure test.
Broken magnet → each piece still has N and S (poles never isolated).
Freely suspended magnet points North–South → basis of the compass; Earth is a magnet.
Natural magnet = magnetite/lodestone.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Repulsion** — not attraction — is the sure test of a magnet.
You **cannot get a single (isolated) pole**; breaking a magnet gives smaller magnets, each with two poles.
**Nickel and cobalt are magnetic** materials along with iron.
A freely suspended magnet rests **North–South**, not East–West.
